newsitem.title: FRANCE: French insurer GAN plunges to loss.
newsitem.headline: French insurer GAN plunges to loss.

text.p: French state-controlled insurer GAN , hit by fresh property losses, reported on Wednesday a nearly 1 billion French franc ($193 million) first-half loss and warned it would need more state money before being privatised.
GAN, which has already generated a flood of red ink, said its net consolidated loss ballooned to 965 million francs ($188 million) from a loss of 387 million francs (75 million) a year earlier.
"This result shows the continued deterioration of the real estate market and efforts by the group to clean up its books," the insurer said.

Chairman Jean-Jacques Bonnaud, who forecast last April GAN would break even in 1996, said it would post a full-year loss but "not necessarily double" the first-half figure. "It's clear these losses ... are a disappointment," he told a news conference.

The performance reflected losses totalling 1.8 billion francs ($350 million) from GAN's real estate banking activities which Bonnaud warned could hit the same level in the second half. But the insurer showed a recovery in its core insurance operations.

Bonnaud would not say how much more state money the insurer might need to ready it for sale. Last year, he raised the possiblity of the need for a 10 billion franc ($1.9 billion) injection. Since then GAN received a 2.8 billion franc ($544 million) recapitalization.
GAN is the latest of a series of French state companies to put its hand out to taxpayers ahead of privatisation.
